name: Nirsevimab
drug_class: Long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV fusion (F) protein
route_note: single intramuscular injection for infants before or during their first RSV season; second-season dose for some high-risk children
targets: RSV fusion glycoprotein (prefusion F, site Ø)

discovery.by: MedImmune/AstraZeneca, from a human antibody (D25) isolated by AIMM Therapeutics
discovery.note: Optimised human IgG1 with the YTE Fc mutation (M252Y/S254T/T256E) that extends half-life through FcRn binding.

tagline: One-dose antibody that protects babies from RSV for a whole season
summary: Nirsevimab is a long-acting human monoclonal antibody that binds the prefusion form of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein. A single intramuscular dose protects infants through their first RSV season, cutting medically attended RSV lower respiratory infection by about three-quarters in trials. Unlike palivizumab, it is intended for all infants, not just those at high risk.
mechanism: RSV enters cells when its fusion (F) glycoprotein switches from a metastable prefusion shape to a postfusion shape, merging viral and cell membranes. Nirsevimab binds site Ø at the apex of prefusion F, locking it and neutralising the virus.

Three amino-acid substitutions (YTE) in the Fc region increase binding to the neonatal Fc receptor at acidic pH, recycling the antibody and extending its half-life to about 2–3 months, enough to cover a typical RSV season with one dose.
uses: Prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants entering or born during their first RSV season
Prevention in children up to 24 months who remain vulnerable during their second RSV season

history.title: Phase IIb
history.detail: A trial in healthy preterm infants shows about 70% reduction in medically attended RSV infection (NEJM 2020).

history.title: MELODY
history.detail: The phase III MELODY trial in healthy late-preterm and term infants reports about 75% efficacy.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission approves Beyfortus in October 2022, the first RSV prophylaxis for all infants.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Beyfortus in July 2023, and the US CDC recommends it for all infants under 8 months entering their first season.

history.title: Supply shortage
history.detail: High demand during the 2023–24 US season leads to supply constraints and temporary prioritisation guidance.

history.title: Real-world impact
history.detail: The HARMONIE trial and national programmes in Spain, France and elsewhere report large reductions in infant RSV hospitalisations.

facts: Nirsevimab is one of the first antibodies used as population-wide passive immunisation for all healthy infants.
It is an alternative to maternal RSV vaccination during pregnancy; most infants need only one of the two.

references.title: Hammitt LL et al. Nirsevimab for prevention of RSV in healthy late-preterm and term infants (MELODY). NEJM 2022
